devel_pod_concurrency.decision: Four Pod case slots landed through PR #16659. In its frozen unsplit 22-case cohort, all cases passed and mean action time fell from 363.3s to 289.2s (20.4%); the case envelope fell 29.8%. Pod requests, memory limits and executor sizing stayed fixed. The current required inventory is partitioned differently, so this is not a new port measurement.
devel_pod_concurrency.scope: Two fresh actions per setting, sequential order 2/4/4/2, with all 88 JUnit case executions passing. Input trees, executor properties and case identities are identical; decoded Commands differ only in the case-limit environment variable. All fixtures were distinct, infrastructure was warm, and cleanup completed. Mean setup was 35.2s at two slots and 40.4s at four; setup variation is separate from case concurrency. This small action screen does not establish whole-PR savings, p90, cold-start behavior or a fleet reliability rate. Two-slot action times ranged 335.6–391.1s; four-slot times ranged 285.2–293.1s. One trust probe took 94.5s in the slower control versus 12–17s elsewhere; its wait is not subdivided in existing traces, so that outlier is not attributed to concurrency. Against the faster control alone, the four-slot mean is 13.8% shorter; this is a sensitivity comparison, not a confidence bound.
devel_pod_concurrency.memory_finding: Maximum whole-action memory was 5.07 GiB at two slots and 5.12 GiB at four. Kubelet samples retained at least 4.51 GiB available and sampled up to 5 runtime Pods in the four-slot arm. Before-import/final snapshots contain no FailedScheduling, OOMKilled or eviction reasons. Ten-second sampling and snapshots can miss transient events.

lanes.title: Recover completed RBE results after execution-stream loss
lanes.status: Recovery control complete; diagnostic PR open
lanes.observed: Native Bazel recovered one injected gRPC INTERNAL after its first Operation using one Execute and one same-ID WaitExecution. Two interruptions exhausted remote_retries=1: one physical test passed, but Bazel exited 34 with no TestResult. This is a sufficient false-red mechanism, not proof of the natural RST_STREAM cause.
lanes.measurement: Next natural false-red: private narrowly enabled native remote_grpc_log; summarize first Operation, Execute/WaitExecution statuses and retry consumption, correlate exact provider operation. Separate Wait-only retry budget is an upstream candidate requiring cancellation/Execute replay controls.
lanes.acceptance: Capture the native Execute/WaitExecution sequence and inject a transport reset after the first accepted Operation. Verify recovery of the original result, one physical execution, a native TestResult, and cancellation behavior. Correlate provider/proxy traces where available. Keep remote_retries=1 until cancellation safety is demonstrated; keep raw RPC metadata private.

lanes.title: Validate KVM placement for required Agentplane VM CI
lanes.observed: Seven physical actions / 31 JUnit cases passed. Four KVM actions shared three registered slots; the fourth queued 215.314s and finished 66.668s after the managed VM. Pod finished last, giving zero VM-only fixed-clock headroom. The newer-source repeat is not a matched graph.
lanes.measurement: Run at least three bounded bursts, each equivalent to four concurrent PRs, on literal source pins. Include one after natural scale-down to one registered worker; observe all required GitHub gates and isolation.
lanes.acceptance: Repeat matched cold/warm selected graphs and bounded concurrent admission on the existing pool, recording routing, compatible healthy/busy capacity, queue clocks, source/CAS identity, cleanup and all ordinary VM cases. Obtain actual required-check feedback on the experiment PR. Propose required routing only when complete feedback and capacity evidence support it.

lanes.title: Eliminate avoidable cold Agentplane system-test baseline rebuilds
lanes.status: Reason diagnostic merged; cache repair unproven
lanes.observed: The 12-head census found 36 target opportunities: 18 absent, three unavailable, three cached and 12 fresh suite outcomes, with 15 unique physical IDs. Six of 12 fresh baselines were cold; all cleaned up. Old artifacts did not record why. The merged span records reuse/rebuild reasons without retaining extra mutable state.
lanes.measurement: Collect seven complete UTC days or the first 50 fresh retained-suite outcomes, whichever is later. Keep cached, failed and missing outcomes separate; group by backend, worker, compatibility key, fingerprint and rebuild reason.
lanes.acceptance: Measure natural cold/warm exposure, baseline fingerprints and explicit rebuild reasons. Repair avoidable compatibility-key or retention misses supported by evidence. Preserve fresh namespace, database, root/credentials and workspace identities with certified cleanup. Evaluate probe cadence only with full-case and CPU evidence.

lanes.title: Skip unchanged OCI imports only when the image is usable
lanes.status: Usability guard and warm trial pass; draft PR
lanes.observed: Nine real native usability guard cases passed. Same-worker warm ABBA setup averaged 46.992s control versus 32.216s candidate, 14.776s shorter. Both selected graphs passed the identical 27 cases. Their 458.570s / 472.642s Bazel times are not causal evidence: VM root-image inputs differed and order/cache exposure were unmatched.
lanes.measurement: Keep issue #16028 open. Within seven days after merge or on the next naturally selected backend head, compare matched warm/cold complete graphs and exact-head required gates. Record source/CAS and cache identities, native phases, CPU, peak memory and capacity. Resolve the VM generated-root input mismatch before comparing VM results.
lanes.acceptance: Implement or experimentally reject an import fast path guarded by exact manifest target, correct-platform unpacked filesystem and CRI pin. Exercise same tag/new digest, missing unpack/pin, GC, restart and later Sandbox use. Measure counterbalanced warm/cold lifecycle and selected-graph behavior; source blobs alone are insufficient.

lanes.title: Shorten MCP Actions execution with isolated case resources
lanes.status: Case overlap measured; no action saving
lanes.observed: All five real MCP cases passed in each source-matched ABBA arm. Mean case envelope fell from 112.336s to 96.833s, but whole action grew from 254.348s to 265.866s and CPU also rose. Baselines were warm/warm/warm/cold across different workers. Five peak Sandboxes exactly fit the existing cap; no action, compute or CI win is established.
lanes.measurement: After adoption, collect seven complete UTC days or the first 50 fresh MCP executions, whichever is later. Compare case execution, setup, CPU, scheduling and the last required gate, with cache, retry, baseline-state and tested-source groups kept separate.
lanes.acceptance: Use existing spans to identify the binding phase. Test case-owned OAuth linkage/resources to overlap independent variants, preserving actual login/linkage/tool behavior, the Sandbox cap, cleanup and unique identities. Compare full selected graphs and required CI rather than raising concurrency blindly.

lanes.title: Test read-only harness artifact mounts to avoid OCI unpacking
lanes.status: Real mount feasibility passed; manual draft PR
lanes.observed: Claude and Codex each completed instructed and plain turns in fresh Sandboxes with 44 read-only native artifact mounts and fresh writable homes; cleanup passed. Declared inputs total 914,451,230 bytes versus 914,498,274 packaged, only 47,044 bytes less. One unmatched pair observed less unpack/setup work, but no meaningful input-byte saving or causal CI gain.
lanes.measurement: Keep issue #16030 open. On the next relevant backend head or within seven days of the feasibility pass, compare counterbalanced complete Pod/MCP/VM graphs while retaining real packaged-image boot coverage. Match source/CAS and cache exposure; measure required gates, per-Sandbox mounts, lazy artifact reads and resource cost.
lanes.acceptance: Build a manual real-runtime experiment using pinned declared artifacts, exact paths and executable permissions, fresh writable homes/state and existing isolation. Retain a required real image packaging/boot path. Include RBE input transfer and complete setup/case/cleanup costs; reject the design if those costs or boundary constraints defeat it.

lanes.title: Diagnose and repair silent progress loss in VM CI guests
lanes.status: New QEMU crash classified; original stall unresolved
lanes.observed: A fresh natural failure aborted QEMU at guest uptime 1.773s with an iotlb_to_section assertion; replacement scenario passed but original shutdown receipt was missing. Separate issue #16057 tracks the crash. Two fresh VM passes used three physical actions because one provider pause failed. The original 300s admitted-turn stall did not recur; late live triggers remain unexercised.
lanes.measurement: On the next admitted-turn stall, correlate live samples at 210 and 240 seconds for the same Sandbox UID with Runtime history and independent serial output before cleanup. Review seven days of non-cached physical exposure; the original stall remains open.
lanes.acceptance: Inspect new physical failure artifacts and a comparable pass; attempt a bounded faithful reproduction. Trace the first blocked native operation and repair an established mechanism with a regression. If lifecycle ownership is implicated, map shutdown/reconciliation and simplify one race-tested path. Do not raise timeouts for a wedge.

lanes.title: Diagnose and repair browser login fixture stalls
lanes.status: Controlled auth timeout localized; natural cause open
lanes.observed: Three fresh browser cases passed with six successful auth exchanges (40–131ms). Holding actual TLS OIDC discovery for 5.25s caused AppProcess.authenticate to time out after 5.002s before page interaction, with client, Go and provider phases retained. This faithful hop control does not reproduce the unknown natural cause or show a lower failure rate.
lanes.measurement: Next natural failure: join client trace ID to Go phases and provider path/port to locate first missing hop; seven-day count of non-cached physical setup outcomes, separate cached rows.
lanes.acceptance: Correlate current failure artifacts client → Go app → provider and find the first missing phase; use a bounded targeted reproduction and repair the responsible boundary. Reuse existing logging, preserve real session issuance/OIDC behavior and token/cookie redaction, without generic retries or timeout bumps.

lanes.title: Locate and repair browser history projection lag
lanes.status: Route-lifetime repair and evidence retention merged
lanes.observed: New natural failure had committed/direct/fresh Electric cursor 334 versus DOM 264; its final live GET began 2.298ms after last-route removal. The repair retains the released route until page cleanup and fixes binary-telemetry request classification. Final candidate passed ten fresh physical stream cases, preserving cursor/anchor/draft assertions. Natural recurrence reduction remains unmeasured.
lanes.measurement: Seven days of post-change physical exposure and next natural failure: final request compared with port-specific ingress and Chromium timing; upstream admission determines next owner.
lanes.acceptance: Correlate committed/direct view, fresh Electric snapshot, browser stream/CDP and DOM cursor on fresh failures. Use the first divergent boundary for a deterministic regression and repair while retaining real streaming integration. Preserve immutable per-attempt artifacts so later diagnostics cannot overwrite the causal evidence.

lanes.title: Refresh backend CI cohort and publish ten-lane follow-up measurements
lanes.status: Fresh cohort and both reports prepared
lanes.observed: 159 latest devel-base backend heads include 129 production heads: 124 green, four failed, one cancelled. Green feedback mean is 13m36s, median 11m27s, p90 23m38s. All 24 repeated green heads had earlier failed Bazel checks and account for 43.1% of summed head feedback. This pre-dispatch baseline is not an attributed improvement.
lanes.measurement: After the dispatched changes land, collect seven complete UTC days (extend sparse lane samples to their stated thresholds), keeping cached, missing, cancelled and failed outcomes separate. Recompute exact-head required feedback and fresh physical failure exposure against this pre-dispatch baseline; link the report PR and each result in issue #16034.
lanes.acceptance: Refresh paginated backend PR-head required-check feedback and reliability exposure; verify current rules, tested merge provenance, native outcomes and repeat attempts. Publish reviewed latency/reliability reports through a gh-pages PR with rendered desktop/mobile/light/dark validation and links to all lane tracking issues.
